items.item_text: Current California license as a mental health professional (e.g., LCSW, LMFT, LPCC, Licensed Psychologist), with eligibility to provide clinical supervision as applicable.
Master’s or doctoral degree in social work, psychology, counseling, marriage and family therapy, or a closely related behavioral health field from an accredited institution.
3 years of supervisory experience, including responsibility for both clinical and administrative supervision.
5 years of progressively responsible experience in prevention, community education, behavioral health, sexual violence/child abuse, or a closely related field.

Knowledge of sexual violence and child sexual abuse prevention, trauma-informed practice, and the needs and experiences of survivors of sexual assault and abuse, including an understanding of the broader social, institutional, and cultural factors that influence prevention response.

Utilize your expertise while making a difference in the community and join our compassionate and highly skilled team as a Director of Prevention and Community Education. The UCLA Health Rape Treatment Center (RTC) provides specialized services for child and adult victims of sexual assault and abuse and conducts prevention, education, and professional training designed to reduce sexual violence and strengthen community response. Prevention programming includes education for youth and other community audiences, training and consultation for schools and partner organizations, and collaboration with community and professional systems.

The Director of Prevention and Community Education will report to the Rape Treatment Center Senior Director and provides leadership for RTC’s prevention and community education programs. The Director will play a key role in strengthening existing initiatives, expanding the reach and impact of prevention efforts, developing innovative programming, and building partnerships to advance RTC's mission.
Provides clinical and administrative supervision and directs day-to-day program operations and staff
Establishes program priorities and quality standards
Oversees prevention initiatives, professional trainings, curriculum development, data, and evaluation
Builds partnerships with schools, law enforcement agencies, and community organizations
Represents the RTC/UCLA Health in community and professional settings
Participates in department leadership, program development, quality improvement, grant activities, and resource development
Ensures that prevention services meet professional, institutional, legal, and funding requirements
Working evenings and weekends on occasion for workshops, trainings, meetings, and community events
We are seeking a dedicated, compassionate, and highly effective leader with:
Exceptional interpersonal judgement and diplomacy.

Ability to clear a Live Scan Fingerprint screening, Criminal Record, Sex Offender Registry, and Child Abuse Index Clearance; per funding agency requirements, and alliances, all staff must complete background checks at least every five years that includes, sex offender registry check, State or FBI criminal history check, including fingerprint check, child abuse and neglect state registry check if available in the state of California.

Demonstrated ability to provide effective clinical and administrative supervision, develop staff, establish clear expectations, address performance concerns, maintain accountability, and foster professional growth.

Knowledge of prevention science, community education, curriculum development, and adult and youth learning, with the ability to translate evidence and best practices into engaging developmentally appropriate, culturally responsive programming for diverse audiences.

Demonstrated ability to provide strategic and creative leadership for a developing program, including identifying opportunities for expansion, designing new initiatives, building sustainable systems and partnerships, and moving ideas from concept through implementation.
